headline: Evaluating long-read assembly and variant calling strategies across data types
label: Long Read Benchmarking And Calibration
summary: Newly posted preprints benchmark long-read SV calling on HiFi and ONT data while new tools target raw nanopore signals and RNA isoform structure.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the evaluation of long-read analysis under data-type-dependent conditions. A preprint benchmarks five local-assembly consensus strategies for long-read human structural variant calling on simulated and real HiFi and ONT data, and reports performance that depends on the data type. Methodological work extends the long-read toolkit in a distinct direction: HARICOT assembles raw nanopore signals without basecalling, using fuzzy de Bruijn graphs and Hough-transform overlap detection, and genomic tessellations introduce a tessellated BWT index intended for faster long-read mapping. Adjacent items address short-read RNA data, where TERRACE 2.0 assembles circular RNAs by combining back-splice and outward-facing paired-end reads, and a published Drosophila study with improved TEChim analysis reports intronic transposons forming alternative exons in brain isoforms, rebutting Azad et al. These items are heterogeneous, so the shared element is calibration and methodological scrutiny rather than a single unified benchmark.
